newsitem.title: THAILAND: Exiles call for unity against Burmese junta.
newsitem.headline: Exiles call for unity against Burmese junta.

text.p: Burmese dissidents on Thursday called for a united effort to fight the military government which displayed its might at annual Armed Forces Day celebrations in Burma's capital of Rangoon.

In a statement to commemorate the 52nd anniversary of Resistance Day -- which the military government calls Armed Forces Day -- a group of student dissidents living in Thailand urged all Burmese to unite against the ruling junta.

"The military is claiming this day as 'armed forces day' and is monopolising the occassion to enshrine the worst aspects of the Burmese army," the All Burma Students' Democratic Front (ABSDF) said in a statement.
About 5,000 soldiers marched and sang through the Burmese capital on Thursday in a parade to show their unity on the country's most important military day.
Burma's top general, Prime Minister Than Shwe, made a speech urging troops to join forces to destroy "destructive elements" inside and outside Burma.
"The army founded in 1945 by General Aung San was established to protect the people. However today it is the people that need protection from the army," the statement from the dissidents said.
"The army has refused to honour the result of the 1990 general election, and continues to commit atrocities and grave human rights violations, and wage wars against the ethnic minorities in Burma."
Aung San spearheaded the fight for Burma's freedom from Britain and was assassinated on the eve of independence.

His daughter is opposition leader Aung San Suu Kyi, whose National League for Democracy (NLD) party won a landslide victory in a 1990 election that was never recognised by the ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC).
The exiles also urged the international community to exert more pressure on the SLORC to respect human rights and democracy.
The SLORC has been accused of human rights abuses by Western governments and human rights organisations.
Earlier this week, the European Union stripped Burma of special trade privileges because of reports Rangoon used forced labour to boost exports.
